Next.js 15 marketing/portal app. Work ONLY in the git worktree /opt/nxeon-wt-mktg (NOT /opt/nxeon). Do NOT run git/npm build/prisma. Edit files only. Do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma, lib/promo-redemption.ts, or lib/tracking.ts (another task owns some of those).

GOAL: Change cookie consent from OPT-IN (tracking blocked until the visitor accepts a banner) to DEFAULT-ON with OPT-OUT (tracking allowed by default; visitor can reject). This is an explicit owner decision to maximize ad-pixel event volume in non-EU markets. Keep it clean and reversible.

STEP 1 — understand the current model:
- Read `lib/consent.ts`. Key: `getCookieConsent()` returns `"all" | "necessary" | null` from the `nxeon_cookie_consent` cookie; `null` = no choice yet. Marketing tags (Meta pixel / Google) load ONLY when consent === "all" (see `components/marketing/ConsentedTags.tsx`). There is also a helper (near the top, ~line 25-33) that decides whether to SHOW the banner.
- Find the banner component: `grep -rln "CONSENT_COOKIE\|cookie consent\|CookieBanner\|nxeon_cookie_consent\|setCookieConsent" components app --include=*.tsx`. Read it. It currently renders a blocking/opt-in cookie banner and calls `setCookieConsent("all"|"necessary")`.

STEP 2 — make the change (DEFAULT-ON):
1. In `lib/consent.ts`: introduce the notion that ABSENCE of an explicit choice means tracking is ALLOWED. The cleanest way: add/adjust a function the gate uses, e.g. `marketingAllowed(): boolean` that returns `getCookieConsent() !== "necessary"` (i.e. allowed unless the visitor explicitly opted out). Do NOT change `getCookieConsent()`'s raw return contract if other code depends on the tri-state — instead add the derived helper and use it in the tag gate. If simpler and safe, you may change the tag gate directly. Keep SSR-safety (returns a safe value on the server).
2. In `components/marketing/ConsentedTags.tsx` (and any other tag gate like ConversionTags/PurchaseTracker if they gate on consent): load the marketing tags when marketing is ALLOWED (not "necessary"), i.e. by default and on "all". Only suppress when the visitor explicitly chose "necessary". Keep the eventual re-measure on the consent-change event.
3. Convert the banner from a blocking opt-in to a **dismissible opt-out notice**: short copy like "We use cookies for analytics and advertising. You can opt out." with two actions — "Reject"/"Opt out" → `setCookieConsent("necessary")`, and "OK"/"Got it" → `setCookieConsent("all")` (and dismiss). It should NOT block the page. Since tracking is now default-on, showing the notice once (until dismissed or a choice is stored) is enough; keep the existing styling/position but make it non-modal and clearly an opt-out (not a gate). Keep a link to the privacy/cookie policy if one exists.
4. Make sure a visitor who previously stored "all" or "necessary" still gets that honored (don't override an explicit choice).

CONSTRAINTS: edit only `lib/consent.ts`, the cookie-banner component, and the tag-gate components (ConsentedTags, and ConversionTags/PurchaseTracker ONLY if they read consent). Do NOT touch schema/promo/tracking-send code. Keep everything typesafe + SSR-safe. Match existing styling.

REPORT (concise): files changed; the exact new default logic (what makes tracking allowed by default); how the banner now behaves (opt-out, non-blocking); confirm an explicit prior "necessary" still blocks tracking and "all" still allows it; and note anything you gated that I should double-check.

content.text:
All changes complete. `useConsentPending.ts` only tracks whether the notice is on screen (so the chat/feedback widgets step aside); since the notice still shows until dismissed, that logic stays correct and needs no change.

## Report

**Files changed** (all in `/opt/nxeon-wt-mktg`):
- `lib/consent.ts`
- `components/marketing/ConsentedTags.tsx`
- `components/marketing/CookieConsent.tsx`

**New default logic (what makes tracking allowed by default)**
- Added `marketingAllowed(): boolean` to `lib/consent.ts`, returning `getCookieConsent() !== "necessary"`. So tracking is allowed when the cookie is absent (`null`, no choice yet) OR `"all"`, and blocked only on an explicit `"necessary"`. `getCookieConsent()`'s tri-state contract is unchanged — the derived helper sits on top of it.
- `ConsentedTags.tsx` now gates on `marketingAllowed()` instead of `getCookieConsent() === "all"`. It still starts `allowed=false` and flips on only after the client mounts, so no marketing script is emitted during SSR, and it still re-measures on `CONSENT_EVENT` (so opting out now removes the tags live, and dismissing keeps them).

**Banner behavior (now opt-out, non-blocking)**
- Converted from an opt-in gate to a dismissible opt-out notice. Copy: "We use cookies … for analytics and advertising … You can opt out any time — it won't affect using the site." with a Privacy policy link retained.
- Buttons: "Opt out" → `setCookieConsent("necessary")`; "Got it" → `setCookieConsent("all")`. Both dismiss and dispatch `CONSENT_EVENT`.
- Changed `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal="false"` to `role="region"` aria-label "Cookie notice". It was already non-modal (wrapper is `pointer-events-none`, only the card is interactive), so it does not block the page; tracking runs regardless of whether the visitor interacts.

**Explicit-choice honoring (confirmed)**
- Prior `"necessary"` → `marketingAllowed()` is false → tags stay off. Prior `"all"` → true → tags load. Either stored value hides the notice on load (unchanged `hasCookieConsent()` check). No override of an explicit choice.

**Things to double-check**
- `PurchaseTracker.tsx` reads no consent (it only polls for `window.nxTrack`, which exists once the pixel loads), so it was intentionally left untouched — it now fires by default because the pixel loads by default. That is the intended net effect but worth confirming it matches your expectation.
- `ConversionTags` was not modified — it renders the actual pixels and gates only on operator ids, not consent. The consent gate remains solely in `ConsentedTags`.
- Per instructions I did not run build/lint/tsc. The edits are typesafe and SSR-safe by inspection, but no compiler was run.
